issues.legal_issue: A criminal case should not be quashed under the High Court’s inherent jurisdiction when the allegations are prima facie and material facts or evidence needed to assess the accused’s involvement remain unresolved.
material_facts: The accused was a Deputy Registrar during a period in which more than 102 sale deeds connected with rehabilitation benefits were registered.
Inquiry reports and the charge-sheets alleged that numerous deeds were fraudulent, that fictitious persons were involved, and that the accused had conspired in or abetted the fraud.
The investigation and collection of evidence were incomplete, and the accused’s alleged involvement had not been finally established.
The High Court quashed the FIRs, charge-sheets, and criminal cases; the State appealed.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in quashing the FIRs and charge-sheets because the allegations and the accused’s involvement required consideration on evidence. The appeals were allowed and the High Court’s judgments were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the High Court does not act as a court of appeal or revision and must exercise its inherent power sparingly, carefully, and with caution. It should not ordinarily assess the reliability of allegations or decide a case on incomplete and hazy facts before the evidence has been collected. The Court relied on M.M.T.C. v. Medchl Chemicals & Pharma (P) Ltd., State of Orissa v. Saroj Kumar Sahoo, and Eicher Tractors Ltd. v. Harihar Singh.

predicates.appeal_challenges_quashing_of_criminal_p: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a decision to quash criminal proceedings.
predicates.prima_facie_allegations_of_involvement: The prosecution alleges facts which, if established, connect the accused to the alleged offence.
predicates.evidence_not_fully_collected: The investigation or collection of evidence concerning the alleged involvement remains incomplete.
predicates.involvement_requires_factual_assessment: Assessing the accused’s involvement depends on facts that cannot fairly be resolved without considering evidence.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges the quashing of criminal proceedings, prima facie allegations remain to be tested, and the accused’s involvement requires factual assessment, the proceedings should not be quashed at that stage.

issues.legal_issue: A registering officer’s alleged knowing participation in fraudulent registration cannot be determined solely from the officer’s registration duties or the presumption that official acts were regularly performed, but must be established through evidence.
material_facts: The accused was alleged to have registered sale deeds that involved fictitious vendors or vendees and were used to obtain rehabilitation benefits unlawfully.
The inquiry identified procedural irregularities in registrations, and the charge-sheet alleged that the accused had abetted a criminal conspiracy and misused his position.
The accused contended that his duty was to register documents and that he had no duty to verify title or knowledge of any fraud.
The investigation had not yet collected all evidence concerning the accused’s alleged role, and his knowledge and intent remained unresolved.
issues.conclusion: Whether the accused knew that the deeds were being used for unlawful gain, abetted the alleged crime, or misused his position could be established only by adducing evidence. The prosecution bore the onus of showing his participation in the fraud; the Court made only prima facie observations and did not determine guilt.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the Registration Act requires the registering officer to inquire whether a document was executed by the person it purports to have been executed by and to satisfy himself as to the identity of persons appearing and the authority of representatives, assignees, or agents. Section 81 addresses knowingly or believingly incorrect registration with the requisite intent or knowledge of likely injury. Under Section 114 of the Evidence Act, official acts are presumed to have been performed in accordance with the prescribed procedure, so the prosecution must show that the officer abetted the offence or was a party to the fraud. The Court relied on Jambu Prasad v. Mohammad Nawab Aftab Ali Khan and referred to Section 44 of the Indian Penal Code concerning injury.

predicates.criminal_case_alleges_registering_office: A criminal proceeding alleges that a registering officer participated in or assisted an offence connected with registration.
predicates.alleged_documents_are_fraudulent: The prosecution alleges that documents presented for registration were fraudulent or were used to carry out a fraud.
predicates.officer_knowledge_or_intent_is_unresolve: Evidence has not yet determined whether the officer knew of the fraud or acted with the alleged intent.

issues.definition: When a criminal case alleges that a registering officer assisted in fraud through registration and the officer’s knowledge or intent remains unresolved, the officer’s participation must be established by evidence.
